title: Keyset Pagination with Opaque Cursors
signature: def paginate(rows, limit, after=None, before=None) -> dict
hints: Sort by the pair (created_at, id), newest first. The pair is unique even when two conversations share a timestamp; created_at alone is not.
The cursor stores the boundary row's (created_at, id), not an offset. 'after' means strictly smaller keys, 'before' means strictly larger keys.
For a before-page, take the limit rows closest to the cursor (the oldest of the newer rows), and still return them newest first.
next_cursor exists only if some row is older than the last item. A full page does not mean there is more.
